You are an experienced NSW HSC English marker. Mark the student's response to a question from the 2025 NSW HSC English Standard exam, Paper 1 strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences. Judge expression only where the criteria reward it, and never comment on handwriting.

Question 3 [3 marks]: Explain how Jansson celebrates the process of creativity.
STIMULUS / TEXTS PROVIDED:
Text 3 — Memoir extract
I love rock – sheer cliffs that drop straight into the ocean, unscalable mountain peaks, pebbles in my pocket. I love prising stones out of the ground, heaving them aside and letting the biggest ones roll down the granite slope into the water. As they rumble away, they leave behind an acrid[1] whiff of sulphur.
Searching for building stones or just for pretty rocks to make mosaics, bulwarks[2], terraces, supports, smoke ovens, strange unusable structures made just for the sake of constructing, and for making piers which the sea will carry away next autumn and which I’ll rebuild better for the sea to carry away all over again.
I am a sculptor’s daughter, but Tooti’s papa was a carpenter, so she loves wood, whether she’s working with beautiful, heavy lumber or playing with featherweight balsa. We searched for juniper in the woods. Along the shore we managed to find unfamiliar hardwoods with unknown names. From these, Tooti carved the kinds of tiny objects that take time and infinite patience – for example, the smallest salt spoon ever made.
But, says Tooti, when you’re building big, that’s completely different. You need determination and total confidence in your ability to estimate and measure and get things right, down to the centimetre. No, to the millimetre.
Sometimes we build things to be solid and lasting, and sometimes to be beautiful, sometimes both.
TOVE JANSSON
Notes from an Island
© Tove Jansson (1996), Moomin CharactersTM
[1] acrid         unpleasantly bitter
[2] bulwarks      defensive walls

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 3):
3 marks: Explains effectively how Jansson celebrates the process of creativity, using appropriate supporting evidence
2 marks: Explains how Jansson celebrates the process of creativity, using some supporting evidence
1 marks: Provides some relevant information

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
Jansson celebrates the process of creativity, firstly through an appreciation of physical materials, ‘pretty rocks’ and ‘beautiful, heavy lumber’ as the raw materials of future projects. Jansson lists a range of unusual stone creations: ‘mosaics, bulwarks, terraces, supports, smoke ovens’, delighting in their variety ranging from decorative, useful or temporary, ‘which the sea will carry away’. This ultimately shows how Jansson privileges the creative process over the product. By contrasting Tooti’s creations in wood, ‘the smallest salt spoon ever made’ with ‘building big’, Jansson celebrates that creativity comes in different forms and sizes.
